issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Ride attributes as private (denoted by '-' in the UML: name: String, abbreviation: char). In the solution, the Ride.name attribute is declared public (public String name;), which contradicts the UML visibility. This mismatch could confuse students about the intended encapsulation and attribute visibility (they are instructed to add getters and the UML marks attributes as private).
issues.suggested_fix: Make the Ride.name attribute private to match the UML specification (change 'public String name;' to 'private String name;') so the implementation matches the problem's encapsulation intent. Keep the existing public getter getName() to provide access.
